name: otp-input
description: Fixed-length SMS or email one-time code that submits itself when the last digit lands, shows where you are with a caret, and refuses a wrong code with a shake while letting the next digit start over.
avoidWhen: Do not use for passwords or free-form text; use password-field or text-field. Do not pair onComplete with a separate Verify button for the same code.

ux.behaviour: When the last digit lands, onComplete fires 150 ms later with a confirm haptic; no button to find
ux.why: You see the whole code for a beat and then it just goes

ux.behaviour: The active cell has a thicker ink border and a blinking caret; cells stay left-to-right in RTL layouts
ux.why: You always know which digit is next

ux.behaviour: Each digit pops into its cell (0.8 to 1) with a tick haptic; paste keeps digits only and caps at length
ux.why: Every keystroke is acknowledged, so a missed one is obvious
ux.reducedMotion: Digits appear without the pop; ticks unchanged

ux.behaviour: When isError turns on, the row shakes once, fires reject, keeps the wrong digits visible in red with the message under them, and takes focus back
ux.why: You can see what you typed against what it said, and the keyboard is already up
ux.reducedMotion: No shake; haptic, red border, and text only

ux.behaviour: The next digit typed after a wrong code replaces the whole code, wherever the cursor was
ux.why: Nobody wants to backspace six times before trying again

ux.behaviour: A wrong code's felt state and pending replacement survive rotation, so the refusal is not repeated
ux.why: Turning the phone is not a second mistake

aiHints: Set ContentType.SmsOtpCode on the single field so SMS autofill works
Keep digit boxes LTR even in an RTL layout
Wire onComplete to the verify call; set isError when it fails and clear isError on the next onValueChange
Do not clear the value yourself on error; the field keeps it visible and replaces it on the next digit
Pass onDone only when the code is not auto-submitted
